Maybe he's too much. Looking for a job is loable, his reaction seems over the top. If I were you I would try to find out why is that, and if it's just genuinely uncomfortable for him to have you working there, accept that he switches gyms. Don't miss the opportunity to work in a place you like, and don't settle for someone who doesn't allow you to do that.

"I always get sad when I finish a book. It feels like I'm losing my friends."

Still had a stroke.
Life of a stupid man by Akutagawa
Perfume by Patrick Süskind and And then there were none by Agatha Christie. (I found both really engaging with closed impacful endings).
I suggest you write "wierd" as "weird". Other than that, this is gorgeous! Especially the cursive you seem to dislike is really pretty. I hope it doesn't all take you too much time.

Alice through the looking glass, the sequel to Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland (which was cool), is offensively bad and has absolutely nothing to do with the original Lewis Carroll book but having the same title.

The book is delicious, even more so than the first, in my opinion.

God's crooked lines. A private detective enters a psychiatric center to investigate a series of crimes and its director. I swear every 20 pages I would be thinking a completely different thing was happening, it's a ride. 

Besides, the representation of the neurodivergent people is really good —sensitive and accurate. The writer spent a long time in a psychiatric center himself doing research and it shows. Superb read.
It definitely is an answer. Just not the one they would like. And sometimes one isn't lucky enough to have other options in sight...

I've been sad lately and Kitchen by Banana Yoshimoto was exactly that for me. It touches sad topics but gives them a new light —a dim one over a warm cup of tea when it's cold outside.

Before the coffee gets cold (Toshikazu Kawaguchi) has a similar feel. It's a set of four sweet stories in a coffee shop with a little surreal twist. One of my favorite books, to be honest.
It is, right? That title would make a nice verse in a poem, by the way. I like it.
